instructions: Rinse the 1 cup rice in two or three changes of water, then cover it with cold water and leave it to soak for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely dice 1/2 an onion, 1/2 cup of zucchini and 1/2 cup of carrot. Pull the stems off the 2 shiitake mushrooms and finely chop the caps. Slice 3 scallions, keeping the whites and greens in separate piles.

Heat 1 tbsp of the sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef with the 1/4 tsp salt and the pinch of pepper and break it up with a spoon. Cook for about 2 minutes, until there's no pink left.
Add the onion, zucchini, carrot, mushrooms and scallion whites. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion turns see-through.
Drain the rice and add it to the pot. Stir for about 1 minute, until the grains look a little see-through at the edges.
Pour in 7 cups water and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to medium, partly cover the pot and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.

Scrape the bottom of the pot, turn the heat to low and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the porridge is thick and creamy. Stir often so it doesn't catch. For a thinner porridge, stir in a splash of water.
Stir in the soy sauce and the scallion greens, and cook for 1 minute. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle it into bowls. Drizzle 1/2 tsp sesame oil over each bowl and sprinkle on the sesame seeds. Serve hot.

To keep it, cool the porridge and transfer it to airtight containers. It keeps in the fridge for 3 days. To reheat, warm it in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water, stirring until it's hot all the way through.
method_notes: No readable page is titled sogogi juk. These two are the same dish, sogogi yachaejuk, a beef and vegetable rice porridge. Aaron & Claire fry ground beef and diced vegetables in sesame oil, toast soaked short-grain rice in the pot, then cook it in 7 cups of water for about 18 minutes; Aeri's Kitchen cooks it in 6 cups with half sweet rice and seasons with soy sauce and sesame oil. Neither page shows a rating, so this is a fallback lead. Aaron & Claire season with Korean beef stock powder, which is replaced here by Aeri's soy sauce. Neither page gives storage times, so the 3 day fridge time is a general guideline. The beef cooks well past 160°F in the pot, so there is no thermometer step.
